ESV.1: Then he brought me to the nave and measured the jambs. On each side six cubits  was the breadth of the jambs.
ESV.2: And the breadth of the entrance was ten cubits, and the sidewalls of the entrance were five cubits on either side. And he measured the length of the nave,  forty cubits, and its breadth, twenty cubits.
ESV.3: Then he went into the inner room and measured the jambs of the entrance, two cubits; and the entrance, six cubits; and the sidewalls on either side  of the entrance, seven cubits.
ESV.4: And he measured the length of the room, twenty cubits, and its breadth, twenty cubits, across the nave. And he said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
ESV.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits thick, and the breadth of the side chambers, four cubits, all around the temple.
ESV.6: And the side chambers were in three stories, one over another, thirty in each story. There were offsets  all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side chambers, so that they should not be supported by the wall of the temple.
ESV.7: And it became broader as it wound upward to the side chambers, because the temple was enclosed upward all around the temple. Thus the temple had a broad area upward, and so one went up from the lowest story to the top story through the middle story.
ESV.8: I saw also that the temple had a raised platform all around; the foundations of the side chambers measured a full reed of six long cubits.
ESV.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits. The free space between the side chambers of the temple and the
ESV.10: other chambers was a breadth of twenty cubits all around the temple on every side.
ESV.11: And the doors of the side chambers opened on the free space, one door toward the north, and another door toward the south. And the breadth of the free space was five cubits all around.
ESV.12: The building that was facing the separate yard on the west side was seventy cubits broad, and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length ninety cubits.
ESV.13: Then he measured the temple, a hundred cubits long; and the yard and the building with its walls, a hundred cubits long;
ESV.14: also the breadth of the east front of the temple and the yard, a hundred cubits.
ESV.15: Then he measured the length of the building facing the yard that was at the back and its galleries  on either side, a hundred cubits. The inside of the nave and the vestibules of the court,
ESV.16: the thresholds and the narrow windows and the galleries all around the three of them, opposite the threshold, were paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows (now the windows were covered),
ESV.17: to the space above the door, even to the inner room, and on the outside. And on all the walls all around, inside and outside, was a measured pattern.
ESV.18: It was carved of cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Every cherub had two faces:
ESV.19: a human face toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved on the whole temple all around.
ESV.20: From the floor to above the door, cherubim and palm trees were carved; similarly the wall of the nave.
ESV.21: The doorposts of the nave were squared, and in front of the Holy Place was something resembling
ESV.22: an altar of wood, three cubits high, two cubits long, and two cubits broad.  Its corners, its base,  and its walls were of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
ESV.23: The nave and the Holy Place had each a double door.
ESV.24: The double doors had two leaves apiece, two swinging leaves for each door.
ESV.25: And on the doors of the nave were carved cherubim and palm trees, such as were carved on the walls. And there was a canopy  of wood in front of the vestibule outside.
ESV.26: And there were narrow windows and palm trees on either side, on the sidewalls of the vestibule, the side chambers of the temple, and the canopies.

NKJV.1: Then he brought me into the sanctuary and measured the doorposts, six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other side—the width of the tabernacle.
NKJV.2: The width of the entryway was ten cubits, and the side walls of the entrance were five cubits on this side and five cubits on the other side; and he measured its length, forty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits.
NKJV.3: Also he went inside and measured the doorposts, two cubits; and the entrance, six cubits high; and the width of the entrance, seven cubits.
NKJV.4: He measured the length, twenty cubits; and the width, twenty cubits, beyond the sanctuary; and he said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
NKJV.5: Next, he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits. The width of each side chamber all around the temple was four cubits on every side.
NKJV.6: The side chambers were in three stories, one above the other, thirty chambers in each story; they rested on ledges which were for the side chambers all around, that they might be supported, but not fastened to the wall of the temple.
NKJV.7: As one went up from story to story, the side chambers became wider all around, because their supporting ledges in the wall of the temple ascended like steps; therefore the width of the structure increased as one went up from the lowest story to the highest by way of the middle one.
NKJV.8: I also saw an elevation all around the temple; it was the foundation of the side chambers, a full rod, that is, six cubits high.
NKJV.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits, and so also the remaining terrace by the place of the side chambers of the temple.
NKJV.10: And between it and the wall chambers was a width of twenty cubits all around the temple on every side.
NKJV.11: The doors of the side chambers opened on the terrace, one door toward the north and another toward the south; and the width of the terrace was five cubits all around.
NKJV.12: The building that faced the separating courtyard at its western end was seventy cubits wide; the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length ninety cubits.
NKJV.13: So he measured the temple, one hundred cubits long; and the separating courtyard with the building and its walls was one hundred cubits long;
NKJV.14: also the width of the eastern face of the temple, including the separating courtyard, was one hundred cubits.
NKJV.15: He measured the length of the building behind it, facing the separating courtyard, with its galleries on the one side and on the other side, one hundred cubits, as well as the inner temple and the porches of the court,
NKJV.16: their doorposts and the beveled window frames. And the galleries all around their three stories opposite the threshold were paneled with wood from the ground to the windows—the windows were covered—
NKJV.17: from the space above the door, even to the inner room, as well as outside, and on every wall all around, inside and outside, by measure.
NKJV.18: And it was made with cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces,
NKJV.19: so that the face of a man was toward a palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion toward a palm tree on the other side; thus it was made throughout the temple all around.
NKJV.20: From the floor to the space above the door, and on the wall of the sanctuary, cherubim and palm trees were carved.
NKJV.21: The doorposts of the temple were square, as was the front of the sanctuary; their appearance was similar.
NKJV.22: The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits. Its corners, its length, and its sides were of wood; and he said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
NKJV.23: The temple and the sanctuary had two doors.
NKJV.24: The doors had two panels apiece, two folding panels: two panels for one door and two panels for the other door.
NKJV.25: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the temple just as they were carved on the walls. A wooden canopy was on the front of the vestibule outside.
NKJV.26: There were beveled window frames and palm trees on one side and on the other, on the sides of the vestibule—also on the side chambers of the temple and on the canopies.

NASB.1: Then he brought me to the nave and measured the side pillars; six cubits wide on each side [was] the width of the side pillar.
NASB.2: The width of the entrance [was] ten cubits and the sides of the entrance [were] five cubits on each side. And he measured the length of the nave, forty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits.
NASB.3: Then he went inside and measured each side pillar of the doorway, two cubits, and the doorway, six cubits [high]; and the width of the doorway, seven cubits.
NASB.4: He measured its length, twenty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits, before the nave; and he said to me, 'This is the most holy [place].'
NASB.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits; and the width of the side chambers, four cubits, all around about the house on every side.
NASB.6: The side chambers were in three stories, one above another, and thirty in each story; and the side chambers extended to the wall which [stood] on their inward side all around, that they might be fastened, and not be fastened into the wall of the temple [itself].
NASB.7: The side chambers surrounding the temple were wider at each successive story. Because the structure surrounding the temple went upward by stages on all sides of the temple, therefore the width of the temple [increased] as it went higher; and thus one went up from the lowest [story] to the highest by way of the second [story].
NASB.8: I saw also that the house had a raised platform all around; the foundations of the side chambers were a full rod of six long cubits [in height].
NASB.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers [was] five cubits. But the free space between the side chambers belonging to the temple
NASB.10: and the [outer] chambers [was] twenty cubits in width all around the temple on every side.
NASB.11: The doorways of the side chambers toward the free space [consisted of] one doorway toward the north and another doorway toward the south; and the width of the free space [was] five cubits all around.
NASB.12: The building that [was] in front of the separate area at the side toward the west [was] seventy cubits wide; and the wall of the building [was] five cubits thick all around, and its length [was] ninety cubits.
NASB.13: Then he measured the temple, a hundred cubits long; the separate area with the building and its walls [were] also a hundred cubits long.
NASB.14: Also the width of the front of the temple and [that of] the separate areas along the east [side totaled] a hundred cubits.
NASB.15: He measured the length of the building along the front of the separate area behind it, with a gallery on each side, a hundred cubits; [he] also [measured] the inner nave and the porches of the court.
NASB.16: The thresholds, the latticed windows and the galleries round about their three stories, opposite the threshold, were paneled with wood all around, and [from] the ground to the windows (but the windows were covered),
NASB.17: over the entrance, and to the inner house, and on the outside, and on all the wall all around inside and outside, by measurement.
NASB.18: It was carved with cherubim and palm trees; and a palm tree was between cherub and cherub, and every cherub had two faces,
NASB.19: a man's face toward the palm tree on one side and a young lion's face toward the palm tree on the other side; they were carved on all the house all around.
NASB.20: From the ground to above the entrance cherubim and palm trees were carved, as well as [on] the wall of the nave.
NASB.21: The doorposts of the nave were square; as for the front of the sanctuary, the appearance of one doorpost was like that of the other.
NASB.22: The altar [was] of wood, three cubits high and its length two cubits; its corners, its base and its sides [were] of wood. And he said to me, 'This is the table that is before the LORD.'
NASB.23: The nave and the sanctuary each had a double door.
NASB.24: Each of the doors had two leaves, two swinging leaves; two [leaves] for one door and two leaves for the other.
NASB.25: Also there were carved on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees like those carved on the walls; and [there was] a threshold of wood on the front of the porch outside.
NASB.26: [There were] latticed windows and palm trees on one side and on the other, on the sides of the porch; thus [were] the side chambers of the house and the thresholds.

WEB.1: He brought me to the temple, and measured the posts, six cubits wide on the one side, and six cubits wide on the other side, which was the width of the tent.
WEB.2: The width of the entrance was ten cubits;  and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on the one side, and five cubits on the other side: and he measured its length, forty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits.
WEB.3: Then went he inward, and measured each post of the entrance, two cubits; and the entrance, six cubits; and the width of the entrance, seven cubits.
WEB.4: He measured its length, twenty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits, before the temple: and he said to me, This is the most holy place.
WEB.5: Then he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the width of every side room, four cubits, all around the house on every side.
WEB.6: The side rooms were in three stories, one over another, and thirty in order; and they entered into the wall which belonged to the house for the side rooms all around, that they might be supported, and not penetrate the wall of the house.
WEB.7: The side rooms were wider on the higher levels, because the walls were narrower at the higher levels. Therefore the width of the house increased upward; and so one went up from the lowest level to the highest through the middle level.
WEB.8: I saw also that the house had a raised base all around: the foundations of the side rooms were a full reed of six great cubits.
WEB.9: The thickness of the wall, which was for the side rooms, on the outside, was five cubits: and that which was left was the place of the side rooms that belonged to the house.
WEB.10: Between the rooms was a width of twenty cubits around the house on every side.
WEB.11: The doors of the side rooms were toward an open area that was left, one door toward the north, and another door toward the south. The width of the open area was five cubits all around.
WEB.12: The building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west was seventy cubits wide; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length ninety cubits.
WEB.13: So he measured the house, one hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, with its walls, one hundred cubits long;
WEB.14: also the width of the face of the house, and of the separate place toward the east, one hundred cubits.
WEB.15: He measured the length of the building before the separate place which was at its back, and its galleries on the one side and on the other side, one hundred cubits; and the inner temple, and the porches of the court;
WEB.16: the thresholds, and the closed windows, and the galleries around on their three stories, over against the threshold, with wood ceilings all around, and from the ground up to the windows, (now the windows were covered),
WEB.17: to the space above the door, even to the inner house, and outside, and by all the wall all around inside and outside, by measure.
WEB.18: It was made with cherubim and palm trees; and a palm tree was between cherub and cherub, and every cherub had two faces;
WEB.19: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side. It was made like this through all the house all around:
WEB.20: from the ground to above the door were cherubim and palm trees made: thus was the wall of the temple.
WEB.21: As for the temple, the door posts were squared; and as for the face of the sanctuary, its appearance was as the appearance of the temple.
WEB.22: The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits; and its corners, and its length, and its walls, were of wood: and he said to me, This is the table that is before Yahweh.
WEB.23: The temple and the sanctuary had two doors.
WEB.24: The doors had two leaves each, two turning leaves: two for the one door, and two leaves for the other.
WEB.25: There were made on them, on the doors of the temple, cherubim and palm trees, like as were made on the walls; and there was a threshold of wood on the face of the porch outside.
WEB.26: There were closed windows and palm trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch: thus were the side rooms of the house, and the thresholds.

CSB17.1: Next he brought me into the great hall and measured the jambs; <sup>ⓜ</sup> on each side the width of the jamb was 10½ feet. <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.2: The width of the entrance was 17½ feet, <sup>[3]</sup> and the side walls of the entrance were 8¾ feet <sup>[4]</sup> wide on each side. He also measured the length of the great hall, 70 feet, <sup>[5]</sup> and the width, 35 feet. <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.3: He went inside the next room and measured the jambs at the entrance; <sup>ⓐ</sup> they were 3½ feet <sup>[7]</sup> wide. The entrance was 10½ feet wide, and the width of the entrance’s side walls on each side <sup>[8]</sup> was 12¼ feet. <sup>[9]</sup>
CSB17.4: He then measured the length of the room adjacent to the great hall, 35 feet, and the width, 35 feet. <sup>ⓑ</sup> And he said to me, “This is the most holy place.” <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple; it was 10½ feet thick. The width of the side rooms all around the temple was 7 feet. <sup>[10]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.6: The side rooms were arranged one above another in three stories of thirty rooms each. <sup>[11]</sup> There were ledges on the wall of the temple all around to serve as supports for the side rooms, so that the supports would not be in the temple wall itself. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.7: The side rooms surrounding the temple widened at each successive story, for the structure surrounding the temple went up by stages. This was the reason for the temple’s broadness as it rose. And so, one would go up from the lowest story to the highest by means of the middle one. <sup>[12]</sup> <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.8: I saw that the temple had a raised platform surrounding it; this foundation for the side rooms was 10½ feet high. <sup>[13]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side rooms was 8¾ feet. The free space between the side rooms of the temple
CSB17.10: and the outer chambers was 35 feet wide all around the temple. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.11: The side rooms opened into the free space, one entrance toward the north and another to the south. The area of free space was 8¾ feet wide all around.
CSB17.12: Now the building that faced the temple yard toward the west was 122½ feet <sup>[14]</sup> wide. The wall of the building was 8¾ feet thick on all sides, and the building’s length was 157½ feet. <sup>[15]</sup>
CSB17.13: Then the man measured the temple; it was 175 feet <sup>[16]</sup> long. <sup>ⓘ</sup> In addition, the temple yard and the building, including its walls, were 175 feet long.
CSB17.14: The width of the front of the temple along with the temple yard to the east was 175 feet.
CSB17.15: Next he measured the length of the building facing the temple yard to the west, with its galleries <sup>[17]</sup> on each side; <sup>ⓙ</sup> it was 175 feet. The interior of the great hall and the porticoes of the court —
CSB17.16: the thresholds, the beveled windows, <sup>ⓚ</sup> and the balconies all around with their three levels opposite the threshold — were overlaid with wood on all sides. <sup>ⓛ</sup> They were paneled from the ground to the windows (but the windows were covered),
CSB17.17: reaching to the top of the entrance, and as far as the inner temple and on the outside. On every wall all around, on the inside and outside, was a pattern
CSB17.18: carved with cherubim and palm trees. <sup>ⓜ</sup> There was a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. <sup>ⓝ</sup> Each cherub had two faces:
CSB17.19: a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and a lion’s face turned toward it on the other. They were carved throughout the temple on all sides.
CSB17.20: Cherubim and palm trees were carved from the ground to the top of the entrance and on the wall of the great hall.
CSB17.21: The doorposts of the great hall were square, <sup>ⓑ</sup> and the front of the sanctuary had the same appearance.
CSB17.22: The altar was <sup>[18]</sup> made of wood, 5¼ feet <sup>[19]</sup> high and 3½ feet long. <sup>[20]</sup> It had corners, and its length <sup>[21]</sup> and sides were of wood. <sup>ⓒ</sup> The man told me, “This is the table that stands before the LORD.” <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.23: The great hall and the sanctuary each had a double door, <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.24: and each of the doors had two swinging panels. <sup>ⓕ</sup> There were two panels for one door and two for the other.
CSB17.25: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the great hall like those carved on the walls. There was a wooden canopy <sup>[22]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup> outside, in front of the portico.
CSB17.26: There were beveled windows and palm trees on both sides, <sup>ⓗ</sup> on the side walls of the portico, the side rooms of the temple, and the canopies. <sup>[23]</sup>

NLT.1: After that, the man brought me into the sanctuary of the Temple. He measured the walls on either side of its doorway, and they were 10 1⁄2 feet thick.
NLT.2: The doorway was 17 1⁄2 feet wide, and the walls on each side of it were 8 3⁄4 feet long. The sanctuary itself was 70 feet long and 35 feet wide.
NLT.3: Then he went beyond the sanctuary into the inner room. He measured the walls on either side of its entrance, and they were 3 1⁄2 feet thick. The entrance was 10 1⁄2 feet wide, and the walls on each side of the entrance were 12 1⁄4 feet long.
NLT.4: The inner room of the sanctuary was 35 feet long and 35 feet wide. “This,” he told me, “is the Most Holy Place.”
NLT.5: Then he measured the wall of the Temple, and it was 10 1⁄2 feet thick. There was a row of rooms along the outside wall; each room was 7 feet wide.
NLT.6: These side rooms were built in three levels, one above the other, with thirty rooms on each level. The supports for these side rooms rested on exterior ledges on the Temple wall; they did not extend into the wall.
NLT.7: Each level was wider than the one below it, corresponding to the narrowing of the Temple wall as it rose higher. A stairway led up from the bottom level through the middle level to the top level.
NLT.8: I saw that the Temple was built on a terrace, which provided a foundation for the side rooms. This terrace was 10 1⁄2 feet high.
NLT.9: The outer wall of the Temple’s side rooms was 8 3⁄4 feet thick. This left an open area between these side rooms
NLT.10: and the row of rooms along the outer wall of the inner courtyard. This open area was 35 feet wide, and it went all the way around the Temple.
NLT.11: Two doors opened from the side rooms into the terrace yard, which was 8 3⁄4 feet wide. One door faced north and the other south.
NLT.12: A large building stood on the west, facing the Temple courtyard. It was 122 1⁄2 feet wide and 157 1⁄2 feet long, and its walls were 8 3⁄4 feet thick.
NLT.13: Then the man measured the Temple, and it was 175 feet long. The courtyard around the building, including its walls, was an additional 175 feet in length.
NLT.14: The inner courtyard to the east of the Temple was also 175 feet wide.
NLT.15: The building to the west, including its two walls, was also 175 feet wide. The sanctuary, the inner room, and the entry room of the Temple
NLT.16: were all paneled with wood, as were the frames of the recessed windows. The inner walls of the Temple were paneled with wood above and below the windows.
NLT.17: The space above the door leading into the inner room, and its walls inside and out, were also paneled.
NLT.18: All the walls were decorated with carvings of cherubim, each with two faces, and there was a carving of a palm tree between each of the cherubim.
NLT.19: One face — that of a man — looked toward the palm tree on one side. The other face — that of a young lion — looked toward the palm tree on the other side. The figures were carved all along the inside of the Temple,
NLT.20: from the floor to the top of the walls, including the outer wall of the sanctuary.
NLT.21: There were square columns at the entrance to the sanctuary, and the ones at the entrance of the Most Holy Place were similar.
NLT.22: There was an altar made of wood, 5 1⁄4 feet high and 3 1⁄2 feet across. Its corners, base, and sides were all made of wood. “This,” the man told me, “is the table that stands in the LORD’s presence.”
NLT.23: Both the sanctuary and the Most Holy Place had double doorways,
NLT.25: The doors leading into the sanctuary were decorated with carved cherubim and palm trees, just as on the walls. And there was a wooden roof at the front of the entry room to the Temple.
NLT.26: On both sides of the entry room were recessed windows decorated with carved palm trees. The side rooms along the outside wall also had roofs.

AMP.1: Then he (the angel) brought me to the nave (outer sanctuary) and measured the side pillars; six cubits wide on each side was the width of the side pillar.
AMP.2: The width of the entrance was ten cubits and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on each side; and he measured its length, forty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits.
AMP.3: Then he went inside [the inner sanctuary] and measured each side pillar of the doorway, two cubits, and the doorway, six cubits [high], and the width of the doorway, seven cubits.
AMP.4: He measured the length [of the interior of the inner sanctuary], twenty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits, opposite the nave (outer sanctuary); and he said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place."
AMP.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits [thick, to accommodate side chambers]; and the width of every side chamber, four cubits, all around the temple on every side.
AMP.6: The side chambers were three stories [high], one above another, and thirty chambers in each story; and the side chambers extended to the wall which stood on their inward side all around, so that they would be attached, but not attached to the wall of the temple itself.
AMP.7: The side chambers became wider at each successive level as they encompassed the temple. Because the structure surrounding the temple went higher by stages on all sides of the temple, for that reason the width of the temple increased as it went higher; and thus one went up from the lowest story to the highest one by way of the second story.
AMP.8: I also saw that the temple (house) had a raised platform all around it; the foundations of the side chambers measured a full rod of six long cubits in height.
AMP.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits. But the free space between the side chambers belonging to the temple
AMP.10: and the outer chambers was a width of twenty cubits all around the temple on every side.
AMP.11: The doorways of the side chambers toward the free space were one doorway toward the north and another doorway toward the south; and the width of the free space was five cubits all around.
AMP.12: The building that was in front of the separate area on the side toward the west was seventy cubits wide; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
AMP.13: Then he measured the temple, a hundred cubits long; the separate area and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long.
AMP.14: Also the width of the front of the temple and the separate areas along the east side totaled a hundred cubits.
AMP.15: He (the angel) measured the length of the building along the front of the separate area behind it, with a gallery on each side, a hundred cubits; he also measured the inner sanctuary and the porches (porticoes) of the courtyard.
AMP.16: The thresholds, the latticed windows, and the galleries all around their three stories, opposite the threshold, were paneled with wood all around, and from the ground to the windows (but the windows were covered),
AMP.17: over the entrance, and to the inner room, and on the outside, and on all the wall all around inside and outside, by measurement.
AMP.18: It was carved with [figures of] cherubim and palm trees; so that a palm decoration was between cherub and cherub, and every cherub had two faces,
AMP.19: so that the face of a man was toward the palm decoration on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm decoration on the other side. It was carved [this way] on the entire house (temple) all around.
AMP.20: From the floor to [the space] above the entrance cherubim and palm decorations were carved, and also on the wall of the nave [the Holy Place].
AMP.21: The doorposts of the nave were square; as for the front of the sanctuary, the appearance of one doorpost was like that of the other.
AMP.22: The altar was of wood, three cubits high and two cubits long; and its corners, its base, and its sides were wood. And he said to me, "This is the table that is before the LORD."
AMP.23: The nave (Holy Place) and the sanctuary (Holy of Holies) each had a double door.
AMP.24: Each of the doors had two leaves, two swinging (folding) leaves; two leaves for the one door and two leaves for the other.
AMP.25: And there were carved on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm decorations like those carved on the walls; and there was a threshold of wood on the front of the porch outside.
AMP.26: There were latticed windows and palm decorations on one side and on the other, on the sides of the porch. Thus were the side chambers and the thresholds of the house.

NRSVCE.1: Then he brought me to the nave, and measured the pilasters; on each side six cubits was the width of the pilasters.
NRSVCE.2: The width of the entrance was ten cubits; and the sidewalls of the entrance were five cubits on either side. He measured the length of the nave, forty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits.
NRSVCE.3: Then he went into the inner room and measured the pilasters of the entrance, two cubits; and the width of the entrance, six cubits; and the sidewalls of the entrance, seven cubits.
NRSVCE.4: He measured the depth of the room, twenty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits, beyond the nave. And he said to me, This is the most holy place.
NRSVCE.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits thick; and the width of the side chambers, four cubits, all around the temple.
NRSVCE.6: The side chambers were in three stories, one over another, thirty in each story. There were offsets all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side chambers, so that they should not be supported by the wall of the temple.
NRSVCE.7: The passageway of the side chambers widened from story to story; for the structure was supplied with a stairway all around the temple. For this reason the structure became wider from story to story. One ascended from the bottom story to the uppermost story by way of the middle one.
NRSVCE.8: I saw also that the temple had a raised platform all around; the foundations of the side chambers measured a full reed of six long cubits.
NRSVCE.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits; and the free space between the side chambers of the temple
NRSVCE.10: and the chambers of the court was a width of twenty cubits all around the temple on every side.
NRSVCE.11: The side chambers opened onto the area left free, one door toward the north, and another door toward the south; and the width of the part that was left free was five cubits all around.
NRSVCE.12: The building that was facing the temple yard on the west side was seventy cubits wide; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its depth ninety cubits.
NRSVCE.13: Then he measured the temple, one hundred cubits deep; and the yard and the building with its walls, one hundred cubits deep;
NRSVCE.14: also the width of the east front of the temple and the yard, one hundred cubits.
NRSVCE.15: Then he measured the depth of the building facing the yard at the west, together with its galleries on either side, one hundred cubits. The nave of the temple and the inner room and the outer vestibule
NRSVCE.16: were paneled, and, all around, all three had windows with recessed frames. Facing the threshold the temple was paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows (now the windows were covered),
NRSVCE.17: to the space above the door, even to the inner room, and on the outside. And on all the walls all around in the inner room and the nave there was a pattern.
NRSVCE.18: It was formed of cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces:
NRSVCE.19: a human face turned toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion turned toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved on the whole temple all around;
NRSVCE.20: from the floor to the area above the door, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall.
NRSVCE.21: The doorposts of the nave were square. In front of the holy place was something resembling
NRSVCE.22: an altar of wood, three cubits high, two cubits long, and two cubits wide; its corners, its base, and its walls were of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that stands before the LORD.”
NRSVCE.23: The nave and the holy place had each a double door.
NRSVCE.24: The doors had two leaves apiece, two swinging leaves for each door.
NRSVCE.25: On the doors of the nave were carved cherubim and palm trees, such as were carved on the walls; and there was a canopy of wood in front of the vestibule outside.
NRSVCE.26: And there were recessed windows and palm trees on either side, on the sidewalls of the vestibule.

MSG.1: He brought me into the Temple itself and measured the doorposts on each side. Each was ten and a half feet thick.
MSG.2:
The entrance was seventeen and a half feet wide. The walls on each side were eight and three-quarters feet thick.
He also measured the Temple Sanctuary: seventy feet by thirty-five feet.
MSG.3: He went further in and measured the doorposts at the entrance: Each was three and a half feet thick. The entrance itself was ten and a half feet wide, and the entrance walls were twelve and a quarter feet thick.
MSG.4: He measured the inside Sanctuary, thirty-five feet square, set at the end of the main Sanctuary. He told me, "This is The Holy of Holies."
MSG.5: He measured the wall of the Temple. It was ten and a half feet thick. The side rooms around the Temple were seven feet wide.
MSG.6: There were three floors of these side rooms, thirty rooms on each of the three floors. There were supporting beams around the Temple wall to hold up the side rooms, but they were freestanding, not attached to the wall itself.
MSG.7: The side rooms around the Temple became wider from first floor to second floor to third floor. A staircase went from the bottom floor, through the middle, and then to the top floor.
MSG.8: I observed that the Temple had a ten-and-a-half-foot-thick raised base around it, which provided a foundation for the side rooms.
MSG.9: The outside walls of the side rooms were eight and three-quarters feet thick. The open area between the side rooms of the Temple
MSG.10: and the priests' rooms was a thirty-five-foot-wide strip all around the Temple.
MSG.11: There were two entrances to the side rooms from the open area, one placed on the north side, the other on the south. There were eight and three-quarters feet of open space all around.
MSG.12: The house that faced the Temple courtyard to the west was one hundred twenty-two and a half feet wide, with eight-and-three-quarters-foot-thick walls. The length of the wall and building was one hundred fifty-seven and a half feet.
MSG.13: He measured the Temple: one hundred seventy-five feet long. The Temple courtyard and the house, including its walls, measured a hundred seventy-five feet.
MSG.14: The breadth of the front of the Temple and the open area to the east was a hundred seventy-five feet.
MSG.15: He measured the length of the house facing the courtyard at the back of the Temple, including the shelters on each side: one hundred seventy-five feet. The main Sanctuary, the inner Sanctuary, and the vestibule facing the courtyard
MSG.16: were paneled with wood, and had window frames and door frames in all three sections. From floor to windows the walls were paneled.
MSG.17: Above the outside entrance to the inner Sanctuary and on the walls at regular intervals all around the inner Sanctuary and the main Sanctuary,
MSG.18:
angel-cherubim and palm trees were carved in alternating sequence.
Each angel-cherub had two faces:
MSG.19: a human face toward the palm tree on the right and the face of a lion toward the palm tree on the left. They were carved around the entire Temple.
MSG.20: The cherubim-palm tree motif was carved from floor to door height on the wall of the main Sanctuary.
MSG.21: The main Sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe. In front of the Holy Place was something that looked like
MSG.22: an altar of wood, five and a quarter feet high and three and a half feet square. Its corners, base, and sides were of wood. The man said to me, "This is the table that stands before God."
MSG.23: Both the main Sanctuary and the Holy Place had double doors.
MSG.24: Each door had two leaves: two hinged leaves for each door, one set swinging inward and the other set outward.
MSG.25: The doors of the main Sanctuary were carved with angel-cherubim and palm trees. There was a canopy of wood in front of the vestibule outside.
MSG.26: There were narrow windows alternating with carved palm trees on both sides of the porch.

NIV.1: Then the man brought me to the outer sanctuary and measured the jambs; the width of the jambs was six cubits on each side.
NIV.2: The entrance was ten cubits wide, and the projecting walls on each side of it were five cubits wide. He also measured the outer sanctuary; it was forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
NIV.3: Then he went into the inner sanctuary and measured the jambs of the entrance; each was two cubits wide. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the projecting walls on each side of it were seven cubits wide.
NIV.4: And he measured the length of the inner sanctuary; it was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits across the end of the outer sanctuary. He said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
NIV.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple; it was six cubits thick, and each side room around the temple was four cubits wide.
NIV.6: The side rooms were on three levels, one above another, thirty on each level. There were ledges all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side rooms, so that the supports were not inserted into the wall of the temple.
NIV.7: The side rooms all around the temple were wider at each successive level. The structure surrounding the temple was built in ascending stages, so that the rooms widened as one went upward. A stairway went up from the lowest floor to the top floor through the middle floor.
NIV.8: I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it, forming the foundation of the side rooms. It was the length of the rod, six long cubits.
NIV.9: The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick. The open area between the side rooms of the temple
NIV.10: and the priests’ rooms was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
NIV.11: There were entrances to the side rooms from the open area, one on the north and another on the south; and the base adjoining the open area was five cubits wide all around.
NIV.12: The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
NIV.13: Then he measured the temple; it was a hundred cubits long, and the temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long.
NIV.14: The width of the temple courtyard on the east, including the front of the temple, was a hundred cubits.
NIV.15:
Then he measured the length of the building facing the courtyard at the rear of the temple, including its galleries on each side; it was a hundred cubits.
The outer sanctuary, the inner sanctuary and the portico facing the court,
NIV.16: as well as the thresholds and the narrow windows and galleries around the three of them—everything beyond and including the threshold was covered with wood. The floor, the wall up to the windows, and the windows were covered.
NIV.17: In the space above the outside of the entrance to the inner sanctuary and on the walls at regular intervals all around the inner and outer sanctuary
NIV.18: were carved cherubim and palm trees. Palm trees alternated with cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:
NIV.19: the face of a man toward the palm tree on one side and the face of a lion toward the palm tree on the other. They were carved all around the whole temple.
NIV.20: From the floor to the area above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the outer sanctuary.
NIV.21: The outer sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe, and the one at the front of the Most Holy Place was similar.
NIV.22: There was a wooden altar three cubits high and two cubits square; its corners, its base and its sides were of wood. The man said to me, “This is the table that is before the Lord.”
NIV.23: Both the outer sanctuary and the Most Holy Place had double doors.
NIV.24: Each door had two leaves—two hinged leaves for each door.
NIV.25: And on the doors of the outer sanctuary were carved cherubim and palm trees like those carved on the walls, and there was a wooden overhang on the front of the portico.
NIV.26: On the sidewalls of the portico were narrow windows with palm trees carved on each side. The side rooms of the temple also had overhangs.
